audit.whatIsWrong: Prose (whys[4-6], mid, late) says Rumble owns levels 3-6, first item and late, but the level chart already reads Skill/Rumble/Rumble/Skill/Zaahen/Skill/Zaahen and Zaahen wins 54.09% over 562 games.
audit.why: Chart and prose rendered two different answers. The mirror audit (rumble__zaahen) settled on 2 Rumble / 2 Zaahen / 3 Skill; the chart already matches that, so the prose is the half that is wrong.
audit.corrected: Rumble's genuine window is levels 2-3 (Danger Zone Flamespitter plus two harpoons). From 4 onward Aureate Rush (E, 10s at rank 1) gives Zaahen a real gap-closer, so 4-5 is skill, 6 and two-plus items are Zaahen's.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] carried no real cooldowns and mislabelled Rumble's slow as coming from Scrap Shield.
audit.why: The Equalizer is 130/105/80 and Scrap Shield is a flat 6s; those numbers are what make the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Attach real numbers: R 130s at rank 1, Scrap Shield 6s, Aureate Rush 10s at rank 1, and the Junkyard Titan overheat lockout as the true punish window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text named 'Scrap Shield (E slow via Electro Harpoon)' — Scrap Shield is W and applies no slow; the slow and the Magic Resist shred are both Electro Harpoon (E). The page also never mentioned Zaahen's dash or his 850-range pull.
audit.why: Rumble's W is a shield plus movement burst; the E carries slow + MR shred and he holds 2 charges. Missing-interactions flags that Scrap Shield's speed burst and The Equalizer's terrain both deny Aureate Rush, and that both sides carry displacement.
audit.corrected: State the MR shred on Electro Harpoon (drives the MR item line), state Dreaded Return (W) pulling from 850 — exactly his harpoon range — and Aureate Rush (E) as a 10s dash that his R wall and W speed burst can deny. Overheat is the no-cast window to commit into.

audit.why: Mercury's Treads plus an MR item is right against stacked harpoon shred.

edits.before: Level 6 stays his — The Equalizer zones any trade before you commit, even with your R.
edits.after: Level 6 is yours — Final Retribution heals off his zone; commit once The Equalizer is spent.

edits.before: His first-item AP spike makes his poke and kite out-damage your sustain.
edits.after: Even at first item: his AP poke rises but Eclipse plus Q healing answers it.

edits.before: Late, Rumble's E kite and R zoning keep dictating side-lane fights.
edits.after: Late, your 850-range pull answers his harpoon and closes side lanes.

edits.before: Rumble owns levels 3 through 6: his Flamespitter (Q) heat zone and Electro Harpoon (E) slows keep you out of range with no gap-closer to answer, and at 6 The Equalizer (R) lets him carpet-zone any trade you try to open.
edits.after: Rumble owns levels 2-3: Flamespitter (Q) in Danger Zone plus his two Electro Harpoon (E) charges keep you off the wave. From 4 it evens out — Aureate Rush (E) is a real 10s gap-closer, so step in once his harpoons are spent.

edits.before: He stays ahead into items — his AP poke and E kite outrange your melee sustain and his R dominates fights, so buy MR, dodge his harpoons, and only engage when his heat and E are down.
edits.after: You close it out — Mercury's Treads plus MR blunts the poke, and Dreaded Return (W) pulls from 850, matching his harpoon range. Engage when his harpoons are spent; his R is still 80s at rank 3.

edits.before: Rumble's early lane is oppressive: with Flamespitter (Q) in the heat zone and Scrap Shield (E slow via Electro Harpoon) he zones you off the wave and chunks you every time you step up, and you have no gap-closer to reliably reach him past his Junkyard Titan overheat window.
edits.after: Rumble's early lane is oppressive: Flamespitter (Q) in Danger Zone plus two Electro Harpoon (E) charges zone you off the wave and shred your Magic Resist every time you step up, and Scrap Shield (W) absorbs the burst you need to punish — wait for the Junkyard Titan overheat lockout, when he cannot cast at all.

edits.before: At 6 The Equalizer (R) lets Rumble carpet a huge damage zone over the lane or a fight — even with your R Final Retribution you can't stand in his ult, so he controls where trades happen and pokes you out before you commit.
edits.after: At 6 The Equalizer (R) carpets a damage zone and its wall denies your dash — but it is 130s at rank 1, so once it is spent the lane is yours. Final Retribution heals off the damage you deal, so commit through the window rather than backing off.

edits.before: Rumble's first-item AP spike makes his Flamespitter and Harpoons hurt even more; his heat-managed rotations out-damage your melee sustain, so you farm at range and wait for jungle help rather than solo-diving.
edits.after: Rumble's first-item AP spike makes Flamespitter and Harpoons hurt more, but Aureate Rush (E) is 10s at rank 1 and Scrap Shield (W) is only a 6s shield — dash in on the overheat lockout, pull him with W, and burn the shield down.

edits.before: Rumble keeps kiting you with E slows and R zoning in the side lane, and his teamfight ult is a monster; your path is to itemize MR, dodge the R strip, and threaten him only when his heat and E are on cooldown.
edits.after: Rumble kites with harpoon slows and zones side lanes with R, but Dreaded Return (W) pulls from 850 — the same range as his harpoon — so match his step-up, itemize MR against the shred, and all-in the moment Scrap Shield drops.

edits.before: Probe Rumble's pattern early, then commit your full combo only on his key cooldown — bank knowledge before blood.
edits.after: Electro Harpoon shreds your Magic Resist with every hit, so Mercury's Treads plus an MR item blunts his whole poke pattern.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: The Equalizer is 130s at rank 1 — step out of the flames early.
